r7-weekend-neighbor.title: THE ONE THING: weekend-neighbor gap vs g4/g5 GATING gates
r7-weekend-neighbor.imperative: Determine (a) genuine gap that BLOCKS vs (b) real-but-out-of-scope, given g4/g5 imperatives. Record determination with reasoning.
r7-weekend-neighbor.finding: DETERMINATION: (b) real-but-out-of-scope-for-g3; does NOT bite g4/g5 and does NOT block. Decisive evidence from grip_baseline.py: run_grip_batch calls fit_session_grip_baseline (DB wrapper, whole-session, NO driver-subset param). g4-implement's imperative requires fitting G using ONLY fit-set drivers' laps + held-out scoring on the rest -- that driver split is IMPOSSIBLE through run_grip_batch, so g4 must call the lap-frame seam fit_grip_baseline_from_laps(...laps=...) directly, where weekend_neighbors is a first-class exposed parameter (grip_baseline.py:450). g5-implement's imperative says fit pipeline 'from g2, imported directly -- not a reimplementation' on synthetic injected data; it never routes through run_grip_batch either. Neither GATING harness touches the batch orchestrator, so the batch driver's un-wired weekend_neighbors cannot spuriously degrade their results. Further: g4 fits full-field race sessions on a 3-5 circuit slice (~10 drivers per 50/50 split) and g5 injects realistic fittable field-pooled data, so the thin-session fallback (and thus its neighbor-lookup path) is unlikely to even trigger in their primary evaluation; and if a harness genuinely wanted neighbor extrapolation it can pass weekend_neighbors at the seam it already uses. The implementer flagged this clearly and honestly as triage candidate #1 with correct scoping ('needs an ordered two-pass batch... real design work, not a drop-in'). It IS a real limitation for a future production store-population run via run_grip_batch, correctly deferred to triage, not silently dropped.

Fowler pass clean (2 convention-sanctioned overrides). No blockers.

triage_candidates.statement: run_grip_batch does not wire weekend-sibling-session fits together, so a real production store-population run degrades every thin-session fallback to the degenerate no-neighbor path even when a normal same-weekend fit exists. Needs an ordered two-pass batch (fit normal sessions first per GP, then re-pass thin ones with now-available neighbors). Out-of-scope for g3; does NOT affect g4/g5 GATING gates (neither uses run_grip_batch).

get_grip_at does store.load(year,session_type) then filters gp_name in pandas rather than an indexed single-row query -- fine at current volumes, revisit if a hot-path consumer calls it in a tight loop.
